items.title: Don Menza and Sam Noto interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 28, 1997
items.q: And we were working at The Riverboat. And Joe Romano and I walked in and I had a box of Havana cigars and we had been drinking all day.

ctx.x: matter what you did, you could play really well, but everybody’s, “Well it sure wasn’t much like what Don played.”

You know I played it every night and I had a bag of tricks, and the bag kept getting bigger and bigger, and I had all the space in the world. He never told me, hey cut it short. Never once said that, no matter how long or how absurd or bizarre I got with what I played, he said, “You got it, that’s you.” And people said you have to see him on the drums in back of you — he’s got his foot up on the bass drum and he’s listening and looking at me, laughing you know, and like sometimes he’d egg me on — “yeah, that’s…
He was nuts man. Buddy was a natural guy. He did what he thought at that minute you know?
